title: seclab-vscode broker policy, version 1
description: Per-tab egress and credential policy. Engine-agnostic: it names hosts, ports, schemes, methods and paths, never engine internals. Default is deny.

version.description: Schema major version. Additive optional fields keep 1.

tabId.description: If set, must equal the broker's `SECLAB_TAB_ID`.

baseline.description: Merge the broker's built-in baseline allow rules (extension gallery).

prompt.description: Hold-and-prompt behaviour for requests no rule allows.

enabled.description: When false, unmatched requests are denied at once.

timeoutSeconds.description: A held request is denied when no decision (or JIT credential) arrives in time.

maxPending.description: Open prompts at once; more are denied.

maxHeldFlows.description: Requests held at once, across all prompts and JIT waits.

denyCooldownSeconds.description: After a deny or timeout, the same prompt key is denied without asking for this long. Keeps a polling beacon from becoming a prompt stream.

maxPerMinute.description: New prompts per tab per rolling minute. Beyond this, unmatched requests are denied without a prompt.

offerDenyNewAfter.description: After this many denials (including timeouts) in the broker's session, egress prompts also offer `deny-new-destinations`, which denies every new destination for the rest of the session without asking.

rawIpDestinations.description: Requests to an IP literal that no rule allows. `deny`: denied without a prompt. `prompt-once`: prompted, but only `allow-once` or `deny` is offered, never `allow-tab`.

quietPeriodSeconds.description: Requests made this soon after the tab opened, with no user action yet, are flagged `early-after-open` in prompts and audit.

autoDenyRiskyBeforeUserAction.description: Until the supervisor reports the first user action (`tab.event userAction`), requests to raw IPs and risky destinations are denied without a prompt. This defeats folder-open loaders that need no click.

sentinelMismatch.description: What to do when a sentinel appears anywhere other than the header a matching binding names. It is never swapped either way.

allow.description: Egress allow rules. Anything not matched is held for a prompt, or denied.

credentials.description: Sentinel credentials. A binding does not imply egress: the request must also be allowed.

riskyDestinations.description: Extra risky destinations for this tab, added to the broker's maintained list (see docs/broker-policy.md). Same treatment: no `allow-tab`, auto-deny before the first user action.

id.description: Identifier for rules, credentials and tabs.

host.description: Lowercase ASCII hostname, '*.' + hostname for strict subdomains, or an IPv4/IPv6 literal (no brackets). Non-ASCII names must be given in punycode.

method.description: Upper-case HTTP method, or `*` (any; not allowed in bindings).

path.description: Glob over the decoded, canonical request path (no query). '*' matches within one segment, '**' matches across segments.

rule.description: An egress allow rule. A request matches if every field matches.

id.description: Needed to remove the rule with `policy.update`.

ports.description: Defaults to the scheme's default port.

inject.description: Where and how the real value is written. Some headers are refused; the list is in docs/broker-policy.md.

header.description: The only header the real value is ever written to. Chosen by the host, never by the caller.

fmt.description: Template. '{value}' is the real secret; '{base64:TEXT}' base64-encodes TEXT after substituting {value}. Example: 'Basic {base64:x-access-token:{value}}'.

binding.description: Where a credential may be injected. Matches HTTPS only. Methods must be explicit.

credential.description: A sentinel credential. The broker mints its sentinel (returned by `policy.load`); the host supplies the real value (`credential.provide`).

bind.description: One binding or a list of bindings.

inject.description: Default for bindings without their own `inject`.

provider.description: Extra provider backstop deny-list to apply (by name). Providers are also applied automatically by host.

sentinelPrefix.description: Replaces `SECLAB_SNTL_` for clients that check a token format.
